entities.summary: Lexicography is the study of lexicons and the art of compiling dictionaries, with two distinct academic disciplines: practical lexicography and theoretical lexicography. Practical lexicography involves compiling, writing, and editing dictionaries, while theoretical lexicography focuses on the scholarly study of semantic, orthographic, syntagmatic, and paradigmatic features of lexemes. This field has its roots in ancient civilizations, with evidence of dictionary-like texts dating back to ancient Sumeria and Egypt. The development of lexicography played a crucial role in the spread of knowledge during the Renaissance, as dictionaries became widely available and helped to standardize languages. The first modern English dictionary, 'A Dictionary of the English Language,' was published by Samuel Johnson in 1755. Today, lexicography continues to evolve with advances in digital technology, enabling the creation of online dictionaries and thesauri that can be accessed by millions of people worldwide.
